Ex Mixtilinear

GeometryTrianglesCircles
Game: Two circles sit between the line from A to K, the side BC and the circle through all three corners, and their touch points line up in a surprising way.
How to play: Drag the dots A, B, C and K, or focus a dot and use the arrow keys. Tick "Show hint" for more lines, or press "Find equal circles".
Look for the math

Move K along the bottom side and the two circles change shape. Yet the straight line through each circle's two touching points always aims at the same point outside the triangle — and once K is in just the right spot, both circles are exactly as big as the circle outside the triangle.

The two circles

The picture draws triangle ABC, its circumcircle, and its incircle. For a point K on BC, each of the two extra circles touches the line AK, the line BC and the circumcircle from outside. A circle touching two lines has its centre on an angle bisector at K, so the centre is K + t·u for a known direction u. Tangency to the circumcircle gives one quadratic equation in t; its positive root is the circle. The logic test checks both roots and both circles over 180 triangles.

The point the chords aim at

Let M and L be the touching points on BC and AK. The page's main claim is that both lines ML pass through the excenter E opposite A, and that the line joining the two circle centres passes through E too. This was tested for every generated triangle and every K; it held to floating-point precision. It is the outward-touching version of a fact behind Sawayama's Lemma.

The special spot for K

When K is where the incircle touches BC, both circles have the radius r_a of the excircle centred at E. Press Find equal circles to jump there. The test confirms this for all 180 triangles: the two radii and r_a agree, and the construction's midpoint O is the first circle's centre. The applet signals it by opening its three little eyes; this page writes it in the status line instead. For the inward-touching circles of Thébault's third problem the matching spot is the excircle's contact point, a different case that this applet does not draw.

Two honest quirks

The page calls the midpoint of VH "L", but V and H both lie on BC, and the point that lands at their midpoint is M, the contact on BC. The test checks that version. Also, the applet's quadratic helper refuses a coefficient below 0.01 and then draws no circle at all; this port keeps that behaviour for nearly parallel lines. No rule of the puzzle changes.

Try ticking Show hint, then drag K slowly: watch the two touch-chords keep meeting at E, and see how far the circles travel before their radii match.
